questions.question: Describe the three main layers of the Earth, including the two parts of the core.
questions.expected_answer: Crust: thin rocky outer layer, oceanic about 5-10 km (dense basalt) and continental about 30-70 km (lighter granite). Mantle: about 2 900 km of very hot, dense rock that is mostly solid but flows very slowly. Core: mainly iron and nickel; the outer core is liquid and produces the magnetic field; the inner core is solid because of enormous pressure, at about 5 000-6 000 degrees C.

questions.question: What are tectonic plates, how fast do they move and what causes the movement? Give two pieces of evidence used by Wegener.
questions.expected_answer: Rigid pieces of the lithosphere (crust plus upper mantle) into which the Earth's outer shell is broken. They move about 2-10 cm a year, driven by heat from the interior causing convection currents in the mantle, together with sinking plate edges and spreading at ridges. Evidence: the jigsaw fit of Africa and South America; matching fossils such as Mesosaurus; matching rocks and mountain ranges.

questions.question: Name and describe the three types of plate boundary, with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Divergent: plates move apart and magma forms new crust, e.g. the Mid-Atlantic Ridge or East African Rift. Convergent: plates move together, with subduction of oceanic plates forming volcanoes and earthquakes (Andes) or continental collision forming fold mountains (Himalayas). Transform: plates slide past each other causing earthquakes, e.g. the San Andreas Fault.
